correctness.rationale: After the closed-neighborhood step precisely the Cartesian product of initially empty rows and columns remains unobserved. One empty row or column admits a forcing chain; two of each strand every observed vertex with either zero or at least two unobserved neighbors. Inclusion-exclusion on 0/1 empty rows/columns gives A_mn+A_nm-B. Bernoulli factorial moments equal (m)_r(n)_s(1-p)^(nr+ms-rs); fixed-size moments substitute binomial(mn-nr-ms+rs,t)/binomial(mn,t), whose expansion is valid for m>=n and fixed r,s. These give independent Poisson limits for finite theta; for theta=infinity row mean diverges and row variance is bounded by mean (binomial independence or hypergeometric negative correlation). Direct independent adjacency propagation checked all 4,? subsets of 2x3,2x4,3x3,3x4; exact minimum and boundary cases follow.

final_claim: For R_mn=K_m square K_n, arbitrary sensors power dominate iff there are at most one empty row or at most one empty column. Exact inclusion-exclusion polynomial; Bernoulli p=(log n+c)/m and t=floor(n(log n+c)) fixed budget at ((m-n)log n)/n->theta have two independent Poisson empty-row/column channels and success Phi_c(theta).
